messages:
Alex: Heads up — running a staging apply for branch `secrets-sync` and hit a weird state situation after a simultaneous import. plan shows a resource as both imported and to-be-recreated (ghost metadata). anyone seen this?
Maria: Ugh — can you paste the small plan output or the `terraform state list` lines?
Alex: ```
# plan snippet
~ aws_ssm_parameter.foo (module.app) will be replaced
-/+ aws_ssm_parameter.foo (imported) shows changed metadata keys
```
TJ: That smells like duplicate addresses in state after a partial import. Run `terraform state list | grep ssm` and `terraform state show <address>` for both addresses.
Sam: Also check remote state version and provider version — provider upgrades have caused index shifts for us before.
Alex: Found two entries: `module.app.aws_ssm_parameter.foo` and `aws_ssm_parameter.foo`. The plan toggles annotations on a k8s secret too. When I try `apply` it fails with a lock error: "Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: remote state is locked by ..."
Maria: If it's an orphan lock, `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` will clear it, but confirm no one else is applying. If it's not orphaned, coordinate.
Lucy: For the duplicate resource, `terraform state mv aws_ssm_parameter.foo module.app.aws_ssm_parameter.foo` will canonicalize it. If one is truly stale, `terraform state rm <address>` and then re-import the correct one.
Alex: Did the `state mv` -> moved the address, plan now shows fewer replacements but still a recreate for the k8s secret because helm added a checksum annotation that changed. Any low-risk way to stop churn?
TJ: Short-term: add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` on the `kubernetes_secret` resource to avoid churn while you finish the import. Long-term: make Helm chart stable so it doesn't inject a moving checksum or use a predictable annotation.
Sam: Also confirm provider lockfile — we had provider 3.1.0 -> 3.2.0 rename where `metadata` became `metadata[0]`. That looks like drift but is just schema change. `terraform init -upgrade` + `terraform state replace-provider` can be needed for provider namespace moves.
Alex: Good catch — our `terraform.lock.hcl` had provider pinned older. I'll run `init -upgrade` in a parallel workspace after the force-unlock.
Maria: FYI, if you `terraform state show` and see nearly-identical entries, you can `state mv` then re-run `plan`. If plan still tries to recreate because of annotation differences you can `kubectl annotate` to match expected value before apply.
Alex: Ok plan of attack: 1) confirm nobody else running; 2) force-unlock lock id; 3) `terraform state mv` to canonical address; 4) `terraform init -upgrade` and verify provider; 5) add `lifecycle.ignore_changes` temporarily if helm churn persists; 6) re-run plan and apply. I'll report back.
oncall-bot: deploybot: staging apply queue length 1 — low priority.
Sam: Quick reminder — take a backup of remote state (download) before destructive moves.
Lucy: If anything looks off ping me and I can pair for 10 min. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks all — doing the mv + unlock now, will update in this thread within 15m.
